title: Detroit, Michigan, pictured at night from the International Space Station
description: iss074e0334264 (Feb. 27, 2026) --- Detroit, Michigan—home to America’s automotive pioneers and with a history of more than 300 years—sits on the Detroit River across from Windsor, Ontario, Canada. The International Space Station was orbiting 264 miles above North America at approximately 1:18 a.m. local time when this photograph was taken. Credit: NASA/Chris Williams

title: Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, and Georgian Bay are pictured from the International Space Station
description: iss074e0642367 (May 30, 2026) --- From left, Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, and Georgian Bay figure prominently in this photograph from the International Space Station as it orbited 261 miles above North America. Detroit, Michigan, is at the bottom center near Lake St. Clair, which connects Lake Huron with Lake Erie, partially visible at the bottom. Credit: NASA/Jessica Meir

title: The snow‑capped Himalayas separate Nepal from China
description: iss074e0603570 (May 20, 2026) --- The snow‑capped Himalayas separate Nepal from China in this photograph from the International Space Station as it orbited 259 miles above the Asian mountain range. The range acts as a climate barrier, trapping cooler, moisture‑laden air on the Nepal side and creating a sharp contrast between Nepal’s lush forests and the much drier Tibetan Plateau to the north. Credit: NASA/Jessica Meir

title: Melbourne, Australia, pictured at night from the International Space Station
description: iss074e0491784 (April 14, 2026) --- Melbourne, Australia—home to more than 5.4 million people and known for its highly changeable, continental‑style climate—is pictured at approximately 1:24 a.m. local time from the International Space Station as it orbited 265 miles above the island continent. Credit: NASA/Jessica Meir

title: Turquoise-blue waters of Lake Argentino surrounded by the snow-capped Andes Mountains
description: iss074e0573516 (May 6, 2026) --- Turquoise-blue waters of Lake Argentino are surrounded by the snow-capped Andes Mountains in Los Glaciares National Park in Argentina's Santa Cruz Province. Multiple active glaciers feed the lake with their finely ground glacial sediment giving the lake its striking turquoise‑blue color. The International Space Station was orbiting 269 miles above South America's Patagonia region at the time of this photograph. Credit: NASA/Jessica Meir

title: Cairo, Egypt, pictured at night from space
description: iss074e0790404 (July 1, 2026) --- Cairo, Egypt, and its surrounding metropolitan area—with a population of about 22 million—is split by the Nile River and sits at the base of the Nile Delta. Cairo’s major urban districts (center) use newer LED fixtures that emit bright white light, while the suburban areas (top and bottom) use older high‑pressure sodium (HPS) lamps that produce a warm amber glow. The International Space Station was orbiting 262 miles above Earth at approximately 11:05 p.m. local time when this photograph was taken. Credit: NASA

title: Chennai, on India's southern coast along the Bay of Bengal
description: iss074e0543247 (May 2, 2026) --- Chennai, on India's southern coast along the Bay of Bengal and with a metropolitan population of about 8.7 million, shines with white LED streetlights in this photograph taken at approximately 9:13 p.m. local time from the International Space Station. Credit: NASA/Chris Williams

title: La Malinche Volcano, east of Mexico City
description: iss074e0319896 (Feb. 21, 2026) --- La Malinche Volcano, east of Mexico City, is a dormant, heavily eroded stratovolcano estimated to be about 30 to 35 million years old. The International Space Station was orbiting 259 miles above Oaxaca when this photograph was taken. Credit: NASA/Jessica Meir

title: The Iberian Peninsula, comprised mainly of Spain and Portugal, is pictured from the International Space Station
description: iss075e0225788 (Oct. 14, 2026) --- The Iberian Peninsula, comprised mainly of Spain and Portugal and bounded by the Pyrenees to the northeast (top) and the Strait of Gibraltar to the south (bottom left), is pictured from the International Space Station while orbiting above northern Africa. The microstate of Andorra, the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar, and a small portion of southern France are also part of this geographical landmass in southwestern Europe. Credit: NASA/Anil Menon

title: Dubai's coastline with the famous Palm Isles and The World Islands
description: iss074e0825656 (July 17, 2026) --- Dubai's coastline, an artificial archipelago on the Persian Gulf encompassing the famous Palm Isles and The World Islands, in the United Arab Emirates, is pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited 262 miles above the Middle East. Credit: NASA/Chris Williams

title: Madagascar’s southwestern coast along the Mozambique Channel
description: iss075e0085243 (Aug. 28, 2026) --- Madagascar’s southwestern coast along the Mozambique Channel—characterized by a semi‑arid to desert climate, sandy coastal plains, and shifting dunes—is pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited 263 miles above the African continent. Credit: NASA/Jessica Meir

title: Vitoria lights up the eastern Atlantic coast of Brazil
description: iss074e0459458 (April 9, 2026) --- Vitoria, Brazil, with a metropolitan population of about 1.8 million, lights up the eastern Atlantic coast of the South American nation in this photograph taken at 3:59 a.m. local time from the International Space Station as it orbited 262 miles above. Credit: NASA/Chris Williams
